title: Add prebuilt dashboards for Quickstart Template apps (RAG + agents)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Observability Pack now ships Grafana dashboards tailored to Quickstart Template apps (RAG + agents): latency breakdown, retrieval hit-rate/quality, tool failure rate, and token economics. Dashboards follow the Quickstart tracing/metrics conventions and avoid high-cardinality dimensions by default.
description:
## Summary
Adds a set of Grafana dashboards to the observability-pack for Redwood Quickstart Template apps (RAG + agent loop). The goal is to make “is it working?” and “is it costing too much?” questions answerable out-of-the-box for template users.

Dashboards included:
- **RAG / Agent Overview**: top-level health (req rate, error rate, p95 latency, tokens/sec, top error types)
- **RAG Latency Breakdown**: end-to-end request latency split by phases (gateway/client, model, retrieval, tool execution) using template spans + duration metrics
- **Retrieval Quality & Hit Rate**: retrieval empty-result rate, top-k distribution, hit-rate proxy signals, and latency for retriever + vector store adapter
- **Tool Failures**: tool call rate, tool error rate, tool timeout rate, and p95 tool execution latency; includes “top tool names” panel with guardrails
- **Token Economics**: input/output token distributions, cost proxy panels (tokens per request, tokens per successful request), cache hit proxy if emitted

## Motivation
DevEx templates are meant to be production-minded by default. That only works if the default instrumentation is paired with a default set of dashboards that:
- match template conventions (span names/attributes, metric names)
- are safe to ship broadly (no PII, controlled cardinality)
- are useful for both PLG users (Hosted) and platform teams (Dedicated/Private)

This PR is intentionally **dashboards-only**. Alert rules/SLO examples are in follow-up PR #157.

## Implementation details
- Dashboards are authored as Grafana JSON and wired into the pack’s manifest so they publish with the standard release process.
- Panels assume the template instrumentation emits:
  - request counters + duration histograms
  - token counters/histograms (input/output)
  - retrieval counters + empty-result counters
  - tool execution counters + failure counters
  - trace spans for phase breakdown
- Label strategy:
  - Default group-by dimensions: `service.name`, `deployment.mode`, `model`, `http.route`
  - Optional dimension: `template.name` (present only when user opts into template tagging)
  - Tool name is supported but constrained (see below)

### Cardinality guardrails
To avoid self-inflicted cardinality explosions:
- Tool panels use a **top-N** query and are hidden by default unless `tool.name` cardinality is known to be bounded.
- Retrieval panels avoid per-document labels entirely.
- No panels group by request-id or user identifiers.

## Screenshots
Attached in the PR UI:
- “RAG Latency Breakdown” drilldown
- “Token Economics” distribution panels

## How to test
1) Run a template app with the local collector compose (from the quickstarts repo) and point Prometheus at the exported metrics.
2) Import the dashboards from this pack (or use the pack’s Grafana provisioning).
3) Generate traffic:
   - normal RAG queries
   - queries that produce empty retrieval
   - tool calls that fail/time out (use the tool timeout env var)
4) Validate:
   - Overview panels populate
   - p95 latency matches expectations
   - retrieval empty-result % changes with the test set
   - tool failures appear in “Tool Failures”
   - tokens panels reflect request sizes

## Notes / follow-ups
- Alerts/SLO recommendations in #157.
- If we change metric names in templates, we need to update both this pack and the template observability standard doc to keep dashboards stable.

## Checklist
- [x] Dashboards follow quickstart metrics/tracing conventions
- [x] Panels avoid high-cardinality dimensions by default
- [x] No PII fields included
- [x] Reviewed with Observability/SRE

Refs:
- ENG-4184 (templates observability pack integration)
- Quickstart tracing conventions + template metrics mapping (internal docs)

review_conversation:
Allison Grant: Panels look good and align with the span hierarchy we discussed. Two requests: (1) remove group-by on `http.target` (too many variants) and use `http.route` where possible; (2) please add a note in the dashboards README about tool name cardinality and why top-N is used.

Sergio Costa (author): Good call. Updated queries to prefer `http.route` and added a README section on tool cardinality + a toggle to hide tool-name panels by default.

Christine Wong: +1 on the cardinality stance. Also, can we add a “success-only tokens/request” panel? That’s usually what people want when debugging spend.

Sergio Costa (author): Added “Tokens per successful request” and “Tokens per request (all)” side-by-side in the Token Economics dashboard.

Caleb Johnson: Minor: dashboard variables should default to `service.name` and `deployment.mode` first. Also, avoid `model` variable being mandatory (some users may not tag model consistently).

Sergio Costa (author): Updated variable order and made `model` optional (All value supported). Thanks.

Monica Patel: This is great for template launch. Please ensure filenames and dashboard titles include “Template” so docs can deep-link reliably.

Sergio Costa (author): Renamed dashboard titles + filenames to include “Template” prefix consistently.

Allison Grant: Approved.
Christine Wong: Approved.
Caleb Johnson: Approved.

Merged via squash.
